content.title: About
content.content: Fried tilapia fillet is a tender white-fleshed freshwater fish coated in a crispy golden crust. Tilapia has a mild flavor that pairs well with a variety of spices and sauces. It is usually pan‑fried or deep‑fried and served as a standalone dish or added to salads, sandwiches, and Asian‑style meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tilapia is one of the fastest‑growing farmed fish species, cultivated in more than 50 countries.
Unlike many marine fish, tilapia thrives in fresh water, making its farming relatively simple.
Tilapia is sometimes called “the aquarium fish” because it can be kept easily in home tanks.
Several species exist, but the most common commercial variety is Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
High‑heat frying locks in protein and creates a flavorful, crunchy exterior.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Tilapia provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with many other fish, tilapia contains relatively little saturated fat, fitting well into low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Tilapia offers phosphorus, selenium, and potassium, beneficial for bones, antioxidant defense, and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: Its soft texture and moderate fat content make it gentle on the digestive system, suitable for children and older adults.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including tilapia.

items.title: Omega‑6 fatty acids
items.content: Tilapia is higher in omega‑6 than omega‑3 fatty acids, so regular consumption should be balanced with omega‑3 sources.

items.title: Farming quality
items.content: Poor aquaculture practices can lead to antibiotic or chemical residues in the fish.

items.title: Frying oil
items.content: Repeatedly heated oil can generate trans fats; it is best to fry with fresh oil.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the fried fillet hot, seasoned with salt, pepper, or your favorite spice blend. It works well in salads, tacos, sandwiches, and as a filling for sushi rolls. A squeeze of lemon, tartar sauce, or soy sauce enhances the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fried tilapia in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑top bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven or skillet to restore crispness before serving.
